name: The Offspring
description:
'''The Offspring''' (initially formed under the name '''Manic Subsidal''') is an American [[Rock music|rock]] band formed in [[Garden Grove, California]] in 1984. The band currently consists of lead vocalist and guitarist [[Dexter Holland]], lead guitarist [[Noodles (guitarist)|Noodles]], bassist [[Todd Morse]], multi-instrumentalist [[Jonah Nimoy]], and drummer [[Brandon Pertzborn]]. They played a key role in reviving mainstream interest in punk rock during the 1990s, having sold more than 45 million records and becoming one of the genre's best-selling bands. 

The Offspring achieved a local following with their early releases, including their 1989 album ''[[The Offspring (album)|The Offspring]]'' and the seven-inch EP ''[[Baghdad (EP)|Baghdad]]'' (1991). They signed with independent label [[Epitaph Records]] and released two albums: ''[[Ignition (The Offspring album)|Ignition]]'' (1992) and ''[[Smash (The Offspring album)|Smash]]'' (1994). ''Smash'', which contained the band's first major hit "[[Come Out and Play (The Offspring song)|Come Out and Play]]", is one of the best-selling albums released on an [[independent record label]], selling over 11 million copies worldwide and helping to propel punk rock into the mainstream. The success of ''Smash'' attracted attention from major labels including [[Columbia Records]], with whom the Offspring signed in 1996; their first album for the label, ''[[Ixnay on the Hombre]]'' (1997), did not match its predecessor's success, but received favorable reviews and [[Recording Industry Association of America|gold and platinum]] RIAA certifications. The band reached further success with its fifth album ''[[Americana (The Offspring album)|Americana]]'' (1998), from which three of the singles − "[[Pretty Fly (For a White Guy)]]", "[[Why Don't You Get a Job?]]" and "[[The Kids Aren't Alright]]" − became [[Contemporary hit radio|mainstream radio]] and [[MTV]] staples, while the album went on to sell over five million units in the US and achieved the Offspring's highest chart position on the [[Billboard 200|''Billboard'' 200]], peaking at number two. 

Although the Offspring's first two albums of the 2000s, ''[[Conspiracy of One]]'' (2000) and ''[[Splinter (The Offspring album)|Splinter]]'' (2003), were not as successful as those from the previous decade, both were critically acclaimed, with the former going platinum and the latter being certified gold. The Offspring's eighth studio album, ''[[Rise and Fall, Rage and Grace]]'' (2008), cemented their comeback on the strength of its second single "[[You're Gonna Go Far, Kid]]", which topped the [[Alternative Airplay|''Billboard'' rock charts]] for eleven weeks and has since obtained platinum status. The band released no new studio albums between ''[[Days Go By (The Offspring album)|Days Go By]]'' (2012) and ''[[Let the Bad Times Roll]]'' (2021), but continued touring and released a series of one-off songs in the interim. Their latest studio album, ''[[Supercharged (The Offspring album)|Supercharged]]'', was released in 2024.

The Offspring's longest-serving drummer was [[Ron Welty]], who replaced original drummer [[James Lilja]] in 1987. He was replaced by [[Atom Willard|Adam "Atom" Willard]] in 2003, who himself was replaced four years later by [[Pete Parada]]. Parada parted ways with the band in 2021 after he refused to be [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccinated against COVID-19]], and was officially replaced two years later by Pertzborn. [[Greg K.|Greg "K." Kriesel]] (one of the Offspring's co-founders) was the band's bassist until he was fired in 2018. Kriesel was replaced by Todd Morse, who had been the Offspring's touring guitarist since 2009. Morse's position as touring musician was filled by Nimoy, who later became an official member in 2023.
